text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The government plans a new legislation to force airlines into higher insurance to better protect customers and ensure easier payment of damages.
- Austria has problems co-financing EU-subsidised projects.
- The opposition Green party in the Vienna city parliament demands that the audit office examines Bank Austria's majority shareholder Anteilsverwaltung Zentralsparkasse (AVZ).
- Police have tracked down a 62-year-old man suspected of having sent one of the letters claiming responsibility for the letter bombs over the past few years.
- A majority of Austrians is for the abolition of the country's conscription military service.
- The reformed bankruptcy law is expected to start by September 1.
- The finance ministers of Austria, Germany and Switzerland have called for further budget restructuring and said they are against unfair tax competition within the countries.
- The price of car insurance is expected to fall as competition heats up.

- Germany's energy group Bayernwerk plans to bid for Styria's provincial energy provider Energieholding Steiermark, which is due to be privatised. Federal grid company Verbund and regional provider EVN refuse to cooperate.

- President Thomas Klestil, former chief of staff in the Foreign Ministry, intervened on behalf of the alleged Iranian murderers of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989. The Greens say they have documents to prove it.
- The 1998 budget is expected to contain tax rises as 10 billion schillings are still missing from the budget.
